content.title: Tiger Woods rollover crash: Full list of car wrecks involving golf legend
content.text: World Golf Hall of Fame inductee Tiger Woods showed signs of impairment and was arrested Friday following a car crash in which his Land Rover struck another vehicle and rolled over, Florida authorities said.Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said Woods and the driver of the other vehicle were not injured. Woods was able to crawl out through the passenger side of his vehicle.The crash occurred just after 2 p.m. near Woods' home in Jupiter Island, Florida. Budensiek said Woods attempted to pass a pressure‑cleaning truck on a two‑lane road and swerved to avoid a collision, but clipped the rear of the truck’s trailer. Woods’ vehicle then rolled onto its driver’s side.Investigators at the scene determined Woods was showing signs of impairment, Budensiek said. Woods took a breath test that was negative for alcohol but refused to submit to a urine test. He was charged with driving under the influence (DUI) with property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test, both misdemeanors, the sheriff said.Woods’ manager at Excel Sports has not commented on the incident.This photo provided by the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows the overturned vehicle in a rollover crash which involved Tiger Woods in Jupiter Islan...Tiger Woods' Condition: How Is the Golfer Doing?Martin County Fire Rescue said there were no injuries to those involved in the crash. Budensiek said Woods was being held in jail but separate from others.“He’s not going to be with other inmates that could hurt him or try to capitalize on what he did,” he said. “He’ll pay the price, but he’s not going to pay the price by getting punished in jail.”Woods’ representatives have not commented on the crash.Woods, one of the most accomplished professional golfers in history, has been working his way back to competitive golf following a seventh back surgery in September. He has not announced whether he plans to play in the Masters, scheduled for April 9-12.Tiger Woods Car Crashes: Timeline of Past IncidentsWoods has been involved in several high‑profile vehicle incidents over the years, including crashes in Florida and California and a DUI arrest in 2017.The most serious incident occurred in 2021, when Woods suffered life‑altering injuries that sidelined him from professional golf for months.November 2009: Crash Outside His Home with Elin NordegrenWoods fled his home in Windermere, Florida, early on Nov. 27, 2009, and crashed his Cadillac Escalade into a fire hydrant and a tree in a neighbor’s yard around 2:30 a.m., authorities said.The crash came two days after the National Enquirer published a report alleging Woods had been seeing a New York nightclub hostess and that the two had recently been together in Melbourne. The Windermere police chief at the time said officers arrived to find Woods lying in the street with his then‑wife, Elin Nordegren, standing over him.The chief said Nordegren told officers she was inside the home when she heard the crash and went outside, breaking the rear window of the vehicle with a golf club. Woods suffered lacerations to his upper and lower lips, and officers reported seeing blood in his mouth.May 2017: DUI ArrestWoods was arrested on a driving under the influence charge in 2017 after south Florida police found him asleep behind the wheel of his car with the engine running. The vehicle was stopped in a traffic lane and had damage to the driver’s side, authorities said. Woods later said he had taken a combination of prescription pain medications and experienced an unexpected reaction.He ultimately pleaded guilty to reckless driving and agreed to enter a first‑time DUI offender diversion program. Under the terms of the plea, Woods avoided jail time and was sentenced to one year of probation, fined and ordered to complete community service and a DUI education programThe vehicle driven by Tiger Woods is shown after a crash in Los Angeles in this file photo from February 23, 2021. (AP Images)February 2021: Single‑Car Crash, Leg InjuriesIn February 2021, Woods survived a high‑speed rollover crash after his SUV left a coastal road in Los Angeles County, causing severe injuries to his right leg and ankle.The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said Woods was driving between 84 and 87 mph (135 to 140 kph) on a winding road with a posted speed limit of 45 mph (72 kph) when the vehicle crashed. Investigators did not file charges.Doctors said Woods shattered the tibia and fibula in his lower right leg in multiple places. The injuries were stabilized with a rod inserted into the tibia, while additional fractures to his foot and ankle required screws and pins.Woods spent about three months immobilized, including a period in which a hospital bed was set up in his Florida home, before progressing to crutches and eventually walking on his own. He later said amputation of his right leg “was on the table” during his treatment.Woods did not compete on the PGA Tour in 2021 but returned to tournament play at the Masters in 2022.When Did Tiger Woods and Vanessa Trump Start Dating?Woods and Vanessa Trump, former wife of Donald Trump Jr., began dating privately in late 2024, according to multiple reports. The relationship became public in March 2025, when Woods confirmed it in a social media post.Vanessa Trump has since been seen attending golf events in support of Woods, including recent competitions in Florida. Both have largely kept the relationship out of the public spotlight.Tiger Woods' Net WorthTiger Woods has an estimated net worth of about $1.5 billion, according to Forbes, which lists him among the world’s wealthiest athletes. The vast majority of his fortune has come from endorsements, licensing and business ventures rather than tournament winnings, though he has earned more than $120 million on the PGA Tour. Forbes certified Woods as a billionaire in 2022, citing decades of sponsorship deals, golf‑course design work and investments tied to his global brand.In a polarized era, the center is dismissed as bland.
